semantic_fields.source_context_note: General direction is used as directional context, not a defined trigger. In the example it was assessed partly with net volume (Market Delta) and TICK, which the project does not own; no operational measure is given by the source.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: The source lists 'the market's general direction' as focus element 1 and refers to 'the direction of the general market trend' and 'the market's longer-term (day session) direction' as the direction in which the reversion trade intends to resume movement.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: qualitative 'general direction' of the market. PROJECT: any measure (e.g., a moving average or higher-timeframe trend proxy) would be an INFERRED interpretation, not an EXPLICIT source semantic.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: The concept of a trading range is explicit, but the source gives no general rule for fixing range boundaries; the walk-through boundary is a discretionary bar-level example. The prior-day value-area variant is a Market Profile construct not derivable from 1-minute OHLCV.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'I now view the market as in a trading range defined by the 13:30 lows and the 13:39 highs' (example-specific); reversal trades occur at 'the edges of a trading range (a consolidation area, the value area from the prior day)'; false breakout is 'new highs or lows following an extended trading range'; preopening/opening ranges 'locate the market's estimate of value'.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: range boundaries left to trader discretion / example-specific bars, or value area. PROJECT: any fixed boundary rule would be an INFERRED interpretation; no arbitrary boundary may be promoted to source semantics.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: The concept is explicit, but what makes a bar a 'candidate' high/low (selection rule) is the trader's real-time discretionary declaration, not a defined procedure. In the example it was supported by TICK/volume/offer-volume non-expansion, which the project does not own.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'I declare to myself that the highs of the 13:39 bar are my 'candidate highs' for this bounce'; closing lists 'a candidate price high or low' as focus element 3 and 'an entry that leans on this candidate high or low' as element 4.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: candidate high/low is a discretionary label. PROJECT: any rule for identifying candidate highs/lows would be an INFERRED operationalization, not an EXPLICIT source semantic.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: The morning/opening range is referenced but never defined by exact boundaries (e.g., first N minutes, high/low of a named interval). Observable prices exist, but the source semantics of the boundary are NOT_PINNED.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'Unable to take out yesterday's high, we moved back into the morning range'; the opening range is described as locating 'the market's estimate of value'. No start/end definition of 'morning range' / 'opening range' is given.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: morning range referenced without a definition. PROJECT: any morning-range boundary (e.g., first 30/60 minutes) would be invented, not source-pinned.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: The definition is explicit and largely price/volume-based (new high/low after a range, return to the range; waning volume on the breakout leg). However 'extended trading range' and 'return to that range' are not quantified, and 'limited participation' invokes breadth/participation that is not in the corpus.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'A false breakout occurs when we get new highs or lows following an extended trading range, only to see trade return to that range.' False Upside/Downside Breakout Day: 'The market opens within a range and moves above the range, usually with limited participation and volume that wanes with higher prices, only to fall back into the range and return toward VWAP.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: false breakout = new high/low after a range that reverts into the range; false breakout day = range-open move beyond range with waning volume/participation, reverting toward VWAP. PROJECT: the unquantified 'extended', 'return', and 'limited participation' components would need INFERRED definitions.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Part of the condition is price/volume observable (failure to make new highs; waning volume). The TICK-distribution, TICK-thrust, and offer-side volume components are unavailable inputs. The source presents the integrated read (valuation levels + volume + TICK + price) as the identification method.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: The source's failed-breakout condition integrates several signals: the bounce 'does not expand its TICK distribution and does not expand volume or volume traded at the offer', and price has 'trouble making new highs relative to the 13:39 bar'; a failed opening range breakout is recognized from a momentum/volume peak, a price peak on reduced upside momentum but very strong TICK, then failure of positive TICK to achieve new highs; thrusts in NYSE TICK above 1000 'are no longer able to generate higher prices; there is a stalling out of the rally.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: failed-breakout identification integrates price + volume + TICK + offer-side volume. PROJECT: the TICK/offer-side components are not owned; a price/volume-only subset (new-high failure + waning volume) is observable but is not the source's full condition and is not threshold-pinned.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Return to the range is explicit and price-based, but how far back into the range (extent/touch criterion) is not defined.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'Only to see trade return to that range'; 'moved back into the morning range'; 'only to fall back into the range and return toward VWAP.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: return into the range / toward VWAP. PROJECT: any exact 'returned-to-range' touch threshold would be INFERRED.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: The invalidation reference is explicit: a fresh new high/low beyond the candidate level (or prior day's high) invalidates the reversion read. Exact stop distance above the level is operational detail, not semantic.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'My stop is above the 13:39 highs--a move to new highs invalidates my idea.' 'Unable to take out yesterday's high, we moved back into the morning range.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: new highs/lows beyond the reference invalidate. PROJECT: the invalidation is directly representable from price; only the reference level (candidate high / prior-day high) needs an interpreted definition.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: VWAP is explicitly defined as the volume-weighted average price and is computable from bar price/volume. The session reference is 'the day's VWAP' / 'day session', but the exact computation window (session start) is not pinned by the source; the project would need an explicitly defined project calculation (INFERRED).
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'The volume-weighted average price (VWAP) is an excellent reference point in range bound markets'; 'the day's volume-weighted average price'; 'trading for moves toward VWAP... in range markets and on false breakouts'; 'fade moves away from VWAP that cannot sustain upside/downside price targets.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: VWAP = volume-weighted average price; referenced as the day session's VWAP. PROJECT: computing VWAP from 1-minute OHLCV under an explicitly defined session window is a project calculation (INFERRED window), not an EXPLICIT source window.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: The source's only concrete entry trigger for this family is TICK + Market Delta based and is NOT_OBSERVABLE with current data. The price/volume fade alternative ('fade moves away from VWAP that cannot sustain targets') is not operationally pinned ('cannot sustain' is undefined) and is not a defined entry trigger.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: Explicit entry permission: 'I sell when we make positive TICK readings and green Market Delta readings (more volume at offer than bid) that cannot make fresh price highs.' Price/volume alternative in the template: 'If you are playing a range market, you should fade moves away from VWAP that cannot sustain upside/downside price targets.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: entry requires TICK + Market Delta (explicit); a VWAP fade is mentioned but not operationalized. PROJECT: cannot reproduce the explicit trigger without TICK/Delta; any price/volume-only entry rule would be an INFERRED, not a source-pinned, permission.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Multiple explicit target conventions exist (range lows, VWAP, range midpoint, prior pivot, opposite extreme on sustained strength). The source does not pin one unique primary target for the family; the pivot/value-area variants are undefined or unavailable.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'My profit target is the lows of the trading range'; 'play a reversion back to VWAP as a first target'; reversal 'initial target will generally be the midpoint of that range (which may also be the pivot level from the previous day or week)'; 'a fade back into the day's range is generally a great play for a move back to the VWAP. On sustained strength, those false breaks lead to a complete rotation through the range to the opposite extreme'; 'anticipate a move back to the midpoint of that opening range.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: several target conventions, none uniquely pinned as PRIMARY. PROJECT: choosing one as THE target would be an INFERRED selection, not an EXPLICIT source semantic.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: The range-reversion (fade) trade is explicitly separated from a breakout trade; a breakout is a different setup. This separation is explicit and consistent across posts.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'I'm not playing for a home run breakout trade. If the market moves into breakout mode, I'll consider that a separate trade and setup.' The three-basic-setups taxonomy separates Reversal / Breakout / Continuation; the day-structure taxonomy separates Range Day, Trend Days, Breakout Days, and False Breakout Days, with trading toward VWAP in range/false-breakout conditions and away from VWAP in breakout/trend conditions.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: separation explicit. PROJECT: honoring the separation is source-faithful; merging them would violate source semantics.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Volume's role (confirms/rejects a breakout; wanes on false breakouts; picks up at cover) is explicit, but no numeric thresholds are given for 'dwindling', 'wanes', 'enhanced', or 'picks up'.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: Volume roles are explicit: don't chase highs 'on dwindling volume'; cover when 'one-minute ES volume picks up'; false breakout day has 'volume that wanes with higher prices'; a genuine breakout 'creates enhanced volume on the breakout move'; 'Markets can move out of their ranges, only to fail to attract volume/participation and fall back toward their volume-weighted averages.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: qualitative volume role. PROJECT: any numeric volume threshold or relative-volume baseline would be INFERRED; ordinary 1-minute volume is observable but the source does not pin how it is compared.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Participation/breadth (advance-decline plurality, sector participation, breadth) is explicitly used to distinguish genuine vs false breakouts and to identify range days. This surface is NOT in the Chinese-futures 1-minute OHLCV corpus.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: False breakout days occur 'usually with limited participation'; genuine breakouts require 'the vast majority of sectors should participate in the break, expanding the plurality of advancing or declining stocks'; the range-day template conditions on 'relatively narrow breadth'.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: participation/breadth is a required distinguishing input. PROJECT: not owned; no OHLCV proxy is authorized.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: TICK is explicitly integral to entry, exit, genuine-vs-false breakout identification, and reversal/breakout character. NYSE TICK is NOT owned by the current corpus and is not OHLCV.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: NYSE TICK is integral: entry requires 'positive TICK readings'; cover uses 'very negative (-1000) TICK readings'; reversals on 'very weak/strong NYSE TICK'; breakouts on 'very high/low NYSE TICK levels'; failed opening range breakout from 'failure of positive TICK readings to achieve new highs'; 'thrusts in the NYSE TICK above 1000 are no longer able to generate higher prices.'
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: TICK is an integral input. PROJECT: not owned; treating it as optional or proxying it with OHLCV is forbidden.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Market Delta / bid-vs-offer volume is explicitly integral to the entry/confirmation logic of the flagship walk-through. It is NOT present in 1-minute OHLCV and is not ordinary volume.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: Market Delta (volume at offer vs bid) is integral: entry requires 'green Market Delta readings (more volume at offer than bid)'; candidate-high non-confirmation includes 'does not expand volume or volume traded at the offer'; continuation trades use 'trending cumulative... Market Delta' with 'pullbacks in TICK and Delta' as entries.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: Market Delta is an integral input. PROJECT: not owned; ordinary 1-minute volume is not a faithful substitute.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Sector/index breadth and cross-market confirmation are explicit and integral to the family's identification/confirmation. These surfaces are not in the Chinese-futures corpus.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: Sector non-confirmation is used as counterevidence to an upside breakout (XLE/XLF not confirming; XLB/XLV sketchy at highs); genuine breakouts require leading sectors to lead and 'similar revaluations among related asset classes, such as Treasury instruments, commodities, and currencies'; false breaks can be telegraphed by cross-index non-confirmation ('not confirmed by fresh lows for the NASDAQ or Russell averages'); breakout confirmation includes cross-market repricing.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: sector/cross-market confirmation is an integral input. PROJECT: not owned; no proxy is authorized.

semantic_fields.source_context_note: SOURCE_INSTRUMENT_SCOPE_EXPLICIT = US_EQUITY_INDEX_FUTURES (ES, ER2) + US_INDEX_AND_SECTOR_BREADTH. No source statement mentions Chinese futures or commodity futures as tradeable instruments for this method.
semantic_fields.source_evidence: The source's tradeable instruments in the false-breakout / range-reversion examples are US equity-index futures: ES (S&P 500 E-mini) and ER2 (Russell 2000 futures), in an SPX/NYSE/NASDAQ/Russell context, with US sectors (XLE/XLF/XLB/XLV) and US index breadth.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: scope explicitly US equity-index futures / US index breadth. PROJECT: corpus is Chinese futures (cu/al/ni/au/ag/rb); transfer is NOT source-supported (see instrument-transfer analysis in the dossier).

semantic_fields.source_context_note: Multi-timeframe applicability is explicit, but the source emphasizes 'follow ONE market across many time frames' (same-market multi-timeframe), not multiple markets. No single operating timeframe is pinned (examples use 1-min, 3-min, 30-min bars).
semantic_fields.source_evidence: 'The type of pattern I'm illustrating above occurs on multiple time frames. A key to trading this way is being able to follow one market across many time frames (which is different from following multiple markets in a single time frame)'; 'These [false breakouts] occur at every time frame'; day structure 'trumps longer timeframe trend considerations' for the intraday trader.
semantic_fields.source_vs_project: SOURCE: pattern occurs across time frames of the same market. PROJECT: choosing a specific operating bar-timeframe for the Chinese-futures corpus would be an INFERRED choice; the source does not pin one.
